title: When AI Writes, Who Gets Cited? Evidence of Citation Monoculture Across Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2608.19230v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: As language models move from drafting prose to running literature-search agents with tool calls, fabricated references are becoming easier to catch and constrain. The harder failure begins after every candidate is real: different models may still select the same narrow subset, producing citation monoculture without any single citation being wrong. We isolate this effect on 120 real papers. Eleven models from three vendors choose at most ten papers from uniformly random panels of thirty, with real titles and abstracts but fabricated authors, reassigned years, and hidden venues and citation counts. Each run is compared with indifferent selection on the same panel and realized budget. All eleven models concentrate sharply: the top decile receives 23.3-30.2% of citations against 15.6% under the null, one component explains 68-73% of variation across their preference maps, and cross-vendor agreement nearly matches within-vendor agreement. F

translated_title: 当AI写作时，谁被引用？跨语言模型的引用单一文化证据
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.19230v1 公告类型：交叉 摘要：随着语言模型从起草散文转向运行带有工具调用的文献搜索代理，虚构参考文献变得更容易被捕捉和限制。更困难的失败始于每个候选文献都是真实存在之后：不同模型可能仍会选择相同的狭窄子集，从而产生引用单一文化，而没有任何单个引用是错误的。我们在120篇真实论文上隔离了这种效应。来自三家供应商的十一个模型从三十篇均匀随机的小组中选择最多十篇论文，这些论文具有真实标题和摘要，但作者为虚构的，年份被重新分配，隐藏了期刊和引用次数。每次运行都与同一小组和已实现预算下的无差异选择进行比较。所有十一个模型都显著集中：前十分位数获得23.3-30.2%的引用，而零假设下为15.6%，一个成分解释了它们偏好图中68-73%的变异，跨供应商的一致性几乎与供应商内部的一致性相匹配。
tldr: 本研究揭示，语言模型在引用真实论文时表现出系统性的“引用单一文化”，不同模型倾向于选择相同的狭窄子集，导致引用分布高度集中，且跨供应商间的一致性接近供应商内部一致性。
en_tdlr: This study reveals that language models exhibit systematic "citation monoculture" when citing real papers, as different models tend to select the same narrow subset, leading to highly concentrated citation distributions, with cross-vendor agreement nearly matching within-vendor agreement.
